title: Sequence transduction without recurrence to enable parallelization
description: Dominant sequence transduction models (machine translation, etc.) are based on recurrent neural networks that process tokens step by step. This inherently sequential computation prevents parallelization within a training example and makes learning long-range dependencies expensive, since the number of operations to relate two distant positions grows with their distance. As of the source work, no competitive sequence transduction architecture dispensed with recurrence (and convolution) entirely while still capturing global dependencies between input and output.
canonical_description: no high-performing sequence transduction model avoids recurrence/convolution while modeling long-range dependencies

evidence.quote: The sequential nature of recurrent networks precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths.
